118442.name: Chabad in the Hills - Beverly Hills
118442.note: Jewish Journal, May 21 2014 (Jared Sichel, on the Beverly Hills Hotel boycott): 'A Chabad rabbi, Cunin founded the Beverly Hills Jewish Community in 1997 at the Beverly Hills Hotel' (Rabbi Yossi Cunin; the center's address, 9641 Sunset Blvd, is the hotel's). therebbesimpact.com also has 1997 for Chabad in the Hills. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

117577.name: Chabad of North Hollywood
117577.note: Los Angeles Times, June 18 2012 ('Community at odds over synagogue', Catherine Saillant): 'Chabad of North Hollywood, which has operated a small synagogue in this location since 1981, says the larger structure is needed for a growing congregation' (13079 Chandler Blvd, Sherman Oaks; Rabbi Aaron Abend). A business register's 'est. 2005' for its nonprofit and therebbesimpact.com's 2005 are later than this. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

118283.name: Chabad of SCV
118283.note: COLlive, Feb 16 2021 ('A $1.4 Million Bar Mitzvah in California'): 'For the past 22 years, Shluchim Rabbi Choni and Frumi Marozov arranged many Bar and Bas Mitzvahs in their community in Valencia, California', so about 1999 (therebbesimpact.com: 1998). Counted back, so medium. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

118312.name: Chabad of Mt. Olympus
118312.note: VINnews, Oct 21 2022 (Rabbi Berki Rodal's own account): 'Twenty-four years ago, my wife and I moved to Mt. Olympus, in the beautiful Hollywood Hills, to serve the Jewish community and the large segment of the Russian Jewish population that had moved to the area', so about 1998. Counted back, so medium. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

118202.name: Chabad of the Beach Cities
118202.note: Daily Breeze, Dec 11 2025 (Rabbi Yossi Mintz, 'A Chanukah message: How to secure our future'): 'Rabbi Yossi Mintz is the executive director of the Jewish Community Center–Chabad of the Beach Cities, 2108 Vail Ave., in Redondo Beach. The JCC was founded in 1996'. Its Growing Garden Preschool there is 'Founded: 2000' (Chinuch Office directory 2023-24). Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

118644.name: Chabad Hebrew Center
118644.note: The Attals' Bet Yossef Community Center's About page: 'Rabbi Shmuel and Shaina Attal began implementing the vision in 2003: first offering services in the living room of a humble home, and then moving to a small storefront.' Medium: the page is under the Bet Yossef name (the same rabbi and couple as the Chabad Hebrew Center, 8502 W. Lake Mead Blvd), and therebbesimpact.com has 2002. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

earlier.where: the living room of a humble home

118421.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life
118421.note: Stu News Newport (Aug 2021): 'In its 20 years of service to the community'; founded by Rabbi Reuven Mintz. Counted back. Checked (Nov 6): no second source found. Checked (Nov 7): the 2016-2017 Jewish OC Community Directory (Orange County Jewish Life, http://jlifesgpv.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/JOCCD-2016-FINAL-OCJL-1.pdf): 'Chabad Center for Jewish Life ... Rabbi Reuven Mintz Founded: 2001', so high.

118206.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Mission Viejo
118206.note: The center's Instagram (Apr 2024): Rabbi Zalman Marcus, with his wife Bassie, founded and has directed it 'for the past 28 years', so about 1996; therebbesimpact.com: 1995. Counted back. Checked (Nov 6): no second source found. Checked (Nov 7): the 2016-2017 Jewish OC Community Directory (Orange County Jewish Life, http://jlifesgpv.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/JOCCD-2016-FINAL-OCJL-1.pdf) gives 'Rabbi Zalman Marcus Founded: 1995', a year earlier, so it stays medium.

117549.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Laguna Beach
117549.note: Orange County Jewish Heritage, Feb 1990 (Rabbi David Eliezrie, 'Building Judaism in Orange County, California'): '1984 saw the founding of a satellite center to Chabad of Irvine in Laguna Beach', led then by Rabbi Alter and Binie Tenenbaum. Rabbi Elimelech and Perel Goorevitch came in September 1991 'to continue the establishment of Chabad Laguna Beach' (its own page). (The 2016-17 Jewish OC Community Directory gives 'Founded: 1985' for it under Rabbi Elimelech Goorevitch.)

117553.name: Chabad of Los Alamitos & Cypress
117553.note: Orange County Jewish Heritage, Feb 1990 (Rabbi David Eliezrie, 'Building Judaism in Orange County, California'): 'In mid 1986 Rabbi Yitzchok Marcus began a weekly hike', eight miles each way from Long Beach to Los Alamitos, and residents formed a minyan, Congregation Ahavas Yisroel-Chabad; the Marcuses later moved to Los Alamitos. The listing also covers Cypress: 'In 2002, Rabbi Shmuel and Bluma Marcus founded Chabad Lubavitch of Cypress' (Jewish Long Beach; its own site: 'Since 2003'). (The 2016-17 Jewish OC Community Directory gives 'Founded: 2002' under Rabbi Shmuel Marcus, the year of the Cypress branch.)

earlier.where: Rabbi Yitzchok Marcus walking in from his home in Long Beach to the Los Alamitos minyan

117579.name: Chabad of Westlake Village
117579.note: Thousand Oaks Star, Aug-Nov 1985 (California Digital Newspaper Collection): Rabbi Yitzchok Sapochkinsky first appears in Aug 1985 as 'the newly appointed educational director of Chabad of the [Conejo]', and on Sept 6 1985 Chabad's 'afternoon Hebrew School with newly appointed Rabbi Yitzchok Sapochkinsky as principal will open Wednesday at Suite E 741 [Lakefield Road]' in Westlake Village; his name is not in the paper before 1985 although it covers Chabad from 1977. The name 'Chabad of Westlake Village' (741 Lakefield Road, Suite D) is in the paper from Nov 1993. Medium: in 1985 it was Chabad of the Conejo's Westlake Village branch, and when it took its own name isn't known. (therebbesimpact.com: 1985.) Now at 2524 Townsgate Rd (chabad.org; 530 Hampshire Rd in a 2024 brochure). The Acorn (June 6 2019): 'What started in 1979 as one Westlake Village-based Chabad has blossomed into nine centers from Calabasas to Ventura' — that is Chabad of the Conejo (1979); and (July 2000) its Torah went to its 'new home at 741 Lakefield Road, Westlake Village'.

earlier.where: 741 Lakefield Road, Suites D and E, Westlake Village (from 1985: the Hebrew School; 'Chabad of Westlake Village' there in 1993-1999)

118592.name: Chabad of Topanga
118592.note: Topanga Messenger, June 19 2003 ('Torah, Torah, Torah – Chabad Comes to Topanga', by Susan Chasen; California Digital Newspaper Collection): Rabbi Dovid Weiss called residents as 'Rabbi Weiss from Chabad of Topanga' — 'That's because it's brand new'; 'Dovid and his wife Nechama Dina have just moved to Topanga with their two daughters ... to establish a Chabad center here'; the canyon was unfamiliar to them 'until about two months ago'; it was one of Chabad's '20 new West Coast centers' that year, and for five years before he had been a rabbi at Chabad of Brentwood. Dec 18 2003: 'Rabbi Dovid Weiss who recently established Chabad of Topanga'. Times of Israel (Jan 2025): 'for over 20 years'. The Topanga Historical Society's archive: 'Weiss brought a Chabad to Topanga in 2003'.

earlier.where: the Weisses' rented home on Glen Trail (gatherings at their home or others' houses; the Community House rented for holidays)
